text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The economic group of ministers, meeting under Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri, decided to complete within two weeks arrangements for a new system for importing machinery and heavy plants. Such goods wil be inspected abroad in advance by international companies so that they can pass through Egyptian customs as soon as they arrive.

- Egypt and Jordan will sign six cooperation agreements today. They include agreements on cultural and scientific cooperation, linking the electricity grids, cooperation in animal health and an agreement on postal transfers.

- Industry Minister Soleiman Reda said negotiations are under way with three international establishments to take part in setting up a giant chemical complex in southern Egypt to produce nitrogenous and phosphate fertilisers. The complex would cost three billion pounds ($880 million) and would depend on the phosphates from Abu Tartour.

- It has been decided to set up an international Egyptian company to modernise textile industry techniques and use international management techniques to increase Egyptian exports of textiles and clothes.
- Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily said Egypt was free of beef with mad cow disease.
- Ganzouri said one of the pillars of economic recovery was concern to increase Egyptian exports.
- Ports have been informed of the newly imposed ban on Belgian beef imports.

- The rules and regulations to go with the new investment incentive law will be endorsed this week by Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri. An economic source said the regulations include automatic exemption without intervention by any government department and say that the General Authority for Investment is the body to implement the law.

- The new crimes committe of the council of Arab interior ministers will tomorrow discuss crimes committed through the Internet, which international gangs are using for smuggling drugs and making explosives materials. They will also discuss Israel's use of the Internet to propagate insults against Islam, the Prophet Mohammad and Arabs.
